# Home Innovation Research Labs

> > Home Innovation Research Labs provides building product research, testing, certification services, and the ANSI-accredited National Green Building Standard (NGBS) for the residential construction industry.

Home Innovation Research Labs serves builders, manufacturers, and industry stakeholders with comprehensive research, market analysis, product testing, and green building certification through the NGBS. The organization conducts field evaluations, develops national standards, and provides insights on energy efficiency, accessibility, and sustainable construction practices.

## Key Topics

- National Green Building Standard (NGBS)
- NGBS Green Certification
- Energy Efficiency
- Building Product Testing
- Green Building
- Universal Design & Accessibility
- Building Codes & Standards
- Solar Energy
- Home Construction Research
- Sustainability
- U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)
- Building America Program
- Wildfire Resilience
- Market Research
- Focus Group Research

- [National Standards](https://www.homeinnovation.com/services/national_standards): ANSI-accredited NGBS green building standard and certification services

- [Multiple Units, Multiple Benefits: Multifamily Certification to the NGBS](https://www.homeinnovation.com/insights/blog/multiple-units-multiple-benefits-multifamily-certification-to-the-ngbs/41578): Multifamily construction benefits certified to NGBS green building standard

- [Advanced HVAC Humidity Control for Hot-Humid Climates](https://www.homeinnovation.com/insights/reports/advanced-hvac-humidity-control-for-hot-humid-climates/45397): DOE Building America research on HVAC humidity control for hot-humid climates
- [Field Evaluation of Low-E Storm Windows](https://www.homeinnovation.com/insights/reports/field-evaluation-of-low-e-storm-windows/39447): Field study comparing low-e storm windows energy performance in cold climates
- [Percent Energy Savings: 2009 IECC Analysis](https://www.homeinnovation.com/insights/reports/percent-energy-savings-2009-iecc-analysis/40909): Analysis of 2009 IECC energy code savings and construction cost impacts
- [SolSmart Serves Up Soft Cost Savings](https://www.homeinnovation.com/insights/blog/solsmart-serves-up-soft-cost-savings/42762): DOE's SolSmart program helps builders reduce soft costs for solar energy
